newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU'S SANTER HITS AT RENAULT OVER BELGIAN FACTORY.
newsitem.headline: EU'S SANTER HITS AT RENAULT OVER BELGIAN FACTORY.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer denounced on Saturday as "inexcusable" the way French auto maker Renault SA closed its factory at Vilvorde, Belgium, in February.
"Vilvorde was significant on several counts because the procedures used by Renault were inexcusable," Santer told the daily newspaper Le Monde.

"Without wanting to intervene in the group's strategy, I could not imagine an industry could still act in this way. I thought such methods no longer existed in Europe," he said in reference to the firm's abrupt decision which unions said came as a total surprise.

Santer said the European Commission would soon pronounce on the subject in general, saying employment was a major subject and it was essential Europeans realise the EU was not simply "a single market and single currency...without a social dimension."
"In several major (European) states, there is a risk of confusion in the public's mind between monetary union and unemployment.

"We must put a stop to that notion because monetary union is not a goal in itself but an instrument of economic policy in order to create jobs. We have to fight on two fronts: single currency and the fight against unemployment and in favour of jobs," he said.
Work resumes at Vilvorde on April 14 after a six-week strike to protest against the factory closure which is set for July 31 but could be stopped by court orders.
